title: Oven-Baked Bacon (Tender or Crispy)
subtitle: 400°F oven · One tray, two textures
headnote: Bake bacon together, removing Anthony’s portion while tender and pliable and leaving Mariana’s portion until crispy. Timings are estimates; thickness and oven behavior vary.

ingredientGroups.title: Ingredients & equipment
items: Aluminum foil or parchment paper for lining the pan
Optional: loose foil tent or oven-safe mesh splatter screen

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil or oven-safe parchment for easier cleanup.
Arrange bacon strips flat in a single layer, with a little room between strips. Do not stack them.
Bake uncovered for approximately 13 minutes, then check. For Anthony, remove strips when fully cooked but still tender and flexible, typically around 13–15 minutes for regular-cut bacon.
Continue baking Mariana’s strips for approximately 3–6 minutes more, usually 16–21 minutes total, until nicely browned and crispy. Thin pieces may finish sooner; thick-cut bacon may take longer.
No flipping is required, but optionally turn strips for more even browning. Transfer cooked bacon to paper towels to drain for 1–2 minutes.

To reduce splatter, use a loose tent of foil above the bacon (do not seal) or an oven-safe mesh splatter screen. A tight cover traps steam and reduces crispness; for Mariana’s strips, remove the tent near the end if necessary.
notes: Anthony: prefers tender, pliable bacon—not crunchy. Check early and remove before crisping.
Mariana: prefers crispy bacon. Leave her portion in the oven longer, watching carefully to avoid burning.
A liner beneath the bacon helps cleanup but does not prevent splatter. Use a rimmed baking sheet to contain grease.
Cooking times are starting points, not guarantees; fully cook bacon and judge doneness by appearance and texture.
sourceNote: Family conversation, November 23, 2026. Preferences specifically noted for Anthony and Mariana.
